subject: Post-call: exportable activity records, SOC 2 artifacts & vendor questionnaire
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chan <lisa.chan@summithealth.org>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: exportable activity records, SOC 2 artifacts & vendor questionnaire

Hi Lisa — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and next steps from our call with SummitHealth's IT/security/procurement team:

TL;DR: Redwood can provide admin activity logs (console and API), per-tenant API request logs, and a time-series export suitable for your SIEM. We have SOC 2 Type II evidence and can begin the vendor security questionnaire process.

Notes from the call:
- Requirement: immutable export of admin activity and API logs for 3+ years (retention policy and WORM/immutability controls).
- Use cases: incident investigation, audit evidence for downstream auditors, and periodic data-retention attestations.
- Data scope: admin actions (user/role changes, policy changes), API request/response metadata (no payloads unless requested), and service-level alerts.
- Compliance drivers: SOC 2 for contractual requirement; HIPAA controls for PHI handling; GDPR controls for data subject requests (we discussed pseudonymization and deletion workflows).

What we'll deliver this week (per our commitments):
1) A short SOC 2 artifacts packet (summary + what evidence we can provide) — attached: redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf.
2) Sample export of activity logs in newline-delimited JSON for schema review (attached: activity-logs-sample.jsonl).
3) Copy of our standard vendor security questionnaire template for you to complete, plus a version pre-filled where we can (security fields) — attached: vendor-security-questionnaire-SummitHealth.xlsx.
4) A proposed narrow mutual action plan (MAP): security questionnaire completion by your team -> Redwood returns answers and evidentiary docs -> small technical call on export pipeline and retention (30–45m) -> finalize export format and SLAs.

Next steps / asks for Lisa/Audit team:
- Can you confirm the person who will own the VSQ and the target date to return it? (we suggested EOD next Tue, 2026-04-14)
- Are there specific immutability controls you must see (e.g., HSM-backed WORM buckets, retention locks)? Please list any non-negotiables so we can scope.

Internal note (cc to Sergio/Marissa): Sergio — please review the attached sample log and call out any gaps vs our current export capability (schema, fields retained, retention TTL). Marissa — can you prepare the SOC 2 artifact packet and a one-page summary of what we can and cannot share (evidence that is internal-only vs evidence we can produce for customers)?

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical export call once Lisa confirms the VSQ owner.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

---
Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf (summary), activity-logs-sample.jsonl (schema sample), vendor-security-questionnaire-SummitHealth.xlsx (template)
From: Lisa Chan <lisa.chan@summithealth.org>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: security+procurement@summithealth.org
Date: Sun, 05 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: exportable activity records, SOC 2 artifacts & vendor questionnaire

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap and attachments. A few clarifying questions before we kick off the VSQ:

1) Immutability: Our auditors require retention locks for log exports for at least 3 years and proof that logs cannot be altered once exported. Is Redwood able to write exports to a customer-owned S3 bucket with object lock governance mode enabled? If not, do you provide an HSM-backed WORM store we can reference?

2) Log content: your sample looks good. We need assurances that API request/response bodies are not retained in the export unless explicitly enabled. Also want a field map indicating which fields may contain PII so our DPO can sign off.

3) Export reliability & SLAs: For our purposes we need daily exports with retry/backfill capability for missing days (up to 7 days). Can you confirm typical throughput/latency for generating an export of 30M events/day?

4) VSQ owner: I’ll own the VSQ but will need input from our engineering team; target to return the VSQ is Tue 2026-04-14 (EOD) — we’ll try to be earlier.

Please have your security/engineering SMEs answer the above; I wanted to get these clarified before we schedule the technical call.

Thanks,
Lisa Chan
Lead Security Analyst, SummitHealth
lisa.chan@summithealth.org | +1 617-555-0123
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: exportable activity records, SOC 2 artifacts & vendor questionnaire

Vanessa / Marissa — answering Lisa's numbered items below with what we can commit now and what needs engineering/legal confirmation. I'll also route this to infra/engineering for the technical call.

1) Customer-owned S3 with Object Lock: We support exporting to customer S3 buckets. Current implementation can deliver daily NDJSON exports via push to an S3 URI you provide; customers can enable S3 Object Lock on their side. We do not currently host a managed HSM-backed WORM offering for exports — that would be a product ask. Action: I’ll confirm exact permissions/manifest format required for the S3 target.

2) Log content / PII: By default exports contain metadata only (timestamps, request id, endpoint, response code, user_id hashed). Payloads/prompt text are excluded unless customer explicitly requests full request/response captures and signs a data-processing addendum. I’ve attached the sample mapping (see activity-logs-sample.jsonl) but will produce a field-level map for DPO review.

3) Export reliability & SLAs: We can produce daily exports and support backfill for up to 14 days via our internal backfill job (we typically do 7–14 day backfills for customers). Throughput: 30M events/day export is within typical range — in our internal benchmarks that size compresses to ~12–18GB/day depending on fields included; export generation time for that volume is commonly under 2 hours. Action: engineering to confirm exact time for SummitHealth dataset and confirm retry/backfill SLAs.

Marissa — can you prepare the SOC 2 packet Vanessa attached and add a one-pager about what is customer-exportable vs internal-only? Legal may need to review the data-processing addendum for full capture requests.

I’ll draft a proposed MAP to include these tasks and owners after we get the VSQ back.

- Sergio
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chan <lisa.chan@summithealth.org>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: exportable activity records, SOC 2 artifacts & vendor questionnaire

Hi Lisa — quick note from the SOC/compliance side and next steps attachment.

Attached is a brief SOC 2 artifact packet (redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf) covering the control list we can provide evidence for and a one-page table that indicates which artifacts are shareable versus internal-only. High-level answers to your items:

- Immutability: Redwood supports exporting to customer-managed storage (S3) where customers can enable Object Lock governance/compliance modes. We consider exports written to a customer-owned, Object Lock-enabled bucket to satisfy immutability requirements from an evidence perspective. We will confirm the manifest format and any additional metadata to attest to the immutability (e.g., checksum/signature).
- PII fields: We will deliver a field-level map identifying fields that may contain PII; by default payloads are not included. If SummitHealth requests payload capture, we will coordinate a DPA amendment and technical controls (encryption at rest, restricted retention, auditing).
- SLA/backfill: Our standard Dedicated customers get documented backfill and export SLAs. For hosted accounts we produce daily exports and an ad-hoc backfill job; we will surface SLA language in the MAP so procurement can review.

I attached the files for you to review and marked the rows where we need legal sign-off. Let us know if the VSQ will flag anything we should prioritize.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Compliance Programs | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
